##1.Introduction

This report describes the processing and statistical analysis of DIA proteomics data generated using AlphaDIA. The workflow includes missing value assessment, imputation, normalization, batch correction, quality control, differential expression analysis, and functional enrichment.

##2.Load libraries

```{r}
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(QFeatures)
library(limma)
library(ggplot2)
library(sva)
library(clusterProfiler)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)
library(ReactomePA)
library(pheatmap)
library(data.table)
library(writexl)

```

##3.Load SummarizedExperiment object

```{r}
setwd("Z:/Muskan/Documents/Helsinki/hel_fin_doc/PhD_courses/pc/capstoneProject/alphadia")

se <- readRDS("protein_SE.rds")

assay(se)[assay(se)==0] <- NA
sum(is.na(assay(se)))

```

The protein abundance matrix was imported and zero values were converted back to missing values (NA), since zeros represented proteins that were not detected rather than true zero abundance.

##4.Missing value assesment Missing values per sample

```{r}
sample_na <- colSums(is.na(assay(se)))

barplot(
  sample_na,
  las=2,
  cex.names=0.7,
  main="Missing values per sample"
)
```

##Missing values per protein

```{r}
protein_na <- rowSums(is.na(assay(se)))

hist(protein_na,
     breaks=50,
     main="Missing values per protein")
#Proteins containing missing values in more than 50% of samples were removed.
keep <- protein_na <= (0.5*ncol(se))
se <- se[keep,]

```

##5.Missing value imputation

Three imputation methods were compared.

```{r}
#KNN
se_knn <- impute(se,method="knn")
#MinDet
se_mindet <- impute(se,method="MinDet")
#Zero
se_zero <- impute(se,method="zero")
par(mfrow=c(2,2))

plot(density(na.omit(assay(se))),
     main="Original")

plot(density(na.omit(assay(se_knn))),
     main="KNN")

plot(density(na.omit(assay(se_mindet))),
     main="MinDet")

plot(density(na.omit(assay(se_zero))),
     main="Zero")
```

KNN imputation was selected because it best preserved the original intensity distribution.

##6.Quantile normalization

```{r}
expr_norm <- normalizeBetweenArrays(
    assay(se_knn),
    method="quantile"
)

assay(se_knn) <- expr_norm
#The normalized dataset was saved for downstream analyses.

saveRDS(se_knn,
        "protein_SE_knn_normalized.rds")
```

##7.Principal Component Analysis before batch correction

```{r}
library(ggrepel)
set.seed(456)
expr <- assay(se_knn)

pca_before <- prcomp(
  t(expr),
  center = TRUE,
  scale. = FALSE
)

percentVar <- round(
  100 * pca_before$sdev^2 / sum(pca_before$sdev^2),
  1
)

pca_before_df <- data.frame(
  Sample = colnames(expr),
  PC1 = pca_before$x[,1],
  PC2 = pca_before$x[,2],
  Condition = colData(se_knn)$condition,
  Batch = colData(se_knn)$batch
)

p_before <- ggplot(
  pca_before_df,
  aes(
    PC1,
    PC2,
    color = Condition,
    shape = Batch
  )
) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  xlab(paste0("PC1 (", percentVar[1], "%)")) +
  ylab(paste0("PC2 (", percentVar[2], "%)")) +
  ggtitle("PCA Before Batch Correction") +
  theme_classic()

print(p_before)
```

##8.Batch correction using ComBat

```{r}
se_batch <- se_knn

expr_batch <- ComBat(
  dat = assay(se_batch),
  batch = colData(se_batch)$batch,
  par.prior = TRUE,
  prior.plots = FALSE
)

assay(se_batch) <- expr_batch

saveRDS(
  se_batch,
  "protein_SE_knn_batchcorrected.rds"
)
```

##9.PCA after batch correction

```{r}
expr <- assay(se_batch)

pca_after <- prcomp(
  t(expr),
  center = TRUE,
  scale. = FALSE
)

percentVar <- round(
  100 * pca_after$sdev^2 / sum(pca_after$sdev^2),
  1
)

pca_after_df <- data.frame(
  Sample = colnames(expr),
  PC1 = pca_after$x[,1],
  PC2 = pca_after$x[,2],
  Condition = colData(se_batch)$condition,
  Batch = colData(se_batch)$batch
)

p_after <- ggplot(
  pca_after_df,
  aes(
    PC1,
    PC2,
    color = Condition,
    shape = Batch
  )
) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  xlab(paste0("PC1 (", percentVar[1], "%)")) +
  ylab(paste0("PC2 (", percentVar[2], "%)")) +
  ggtitle("PCA After Batch Correction") +
  theme_classic()

print(p_after)

```

##10. Outlier assessment

```{r}
pca_after_df$Distance <- sqrt(
  pca_after_df$PC1^2 +
    pca_after_df$PC2^2
)

outlier <- pca_after_df[
  which.max(pca_after_df$Distance),
]

outlier
sample_missing <- data.frame(
  Sample = colnames(se_batch),
  Missing = colSums(is.na(assay(se_batch)))
)

sample_missing
#Boxplot
boxplot(
  assay(se_batch),
  las = 2,
  outline = FALSE,
  cex.axis = 0.6,
  main = "Protein Intensities"
)
#Density plot
plotDensities(
  assay(se_batch),
  main = "Density Plot"
)
#MDS plot
plotMDS(
  assay(se_batch),
  labels = colData(se_batch)$condition,
  col = as.numeric(
    factor(colData(se_batch)$condition)
  )
)
```

Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was performed after KNN imputation, quantile normalization, and ComBat batch correction to assess sample clustering and identify potential outliers - One sample (Group1_c-jun_KO_1) showed moderate separation from the remaining samples in the PCA plot. The potential outlier was further evaluated using multiple quality control metrics, including the number of detected proteins, missing values, boxplots, density plots, sample correlation heatmap, and multidimensional scaling (MDS). Although Group1_c-jun_KO_1 had fewer detected proteins than the other samples, its overall intensity distribution and clustering with the c-jun KO group were comparable to the remaining biological replicates. the sample was retained for downstream differential expression and pathway enrichment analyses.

##11.Differential expression analysis

```{r}
saveRDS(se_batch,"protein_SE_knn_batch_corrected_normalized.rds")
expr <- assay(se_batch)
meta <- as.data.frame(colData(se_batch))

design <- model.matrix(~0+condition,data=meta)

colnames(design) <- c(
"c_junKO",
"c_jun_KO_cDDP24h",
"c_jun_KO_cDDP6h",
"Control",
"Control_cDDP24h",
"Control_JNKi24h",
"Control_JNKi6h")

fit <- lmFit(expr,design)
contrast.matrix <- makeContrasts(
Control_vs_KO = c_junKO - c_jun_KO_cDDP24h,
levels=design)

fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fit,contrast.matrix)

fit2 <- eBayes(fit2)

results <- topTable(
fit2,
number=Inf,
adjust.method="BH")
head(results)
summary(results)
write_xlsx(data.frame(Protein_ID = rownames(results), results), "differential_exp_c_junKO_and_c_jun_KO_cDDP24h.xlsx")
```

##12.Volcano plot

```{r}
results$Significant <- "No"

results$Significant[
results$P.Value<0.05 &
abs(results$logFC)>1] <- "Yes"

ggplot(results,
aes(logFC,
-log10(P.Value),
color=Significant))+
geom_point()+
labs(title = "c_junKO vs c_jun_KO_cDDP24h ",
       x = "Log2 Fold Change",
       y = "-Log10(p-value)")+
theme_classic()
ggsave("Volcano_plot_c_junKO_vs_c_jun_KO_cDDP24h.png")
```

##13.Functional enrichment

```{r}
#Gene Ontology
ids <- bitr(
rownames(results),
fromType="UNIPROT",
toType="ENTREZID",
OrgDb=org.Hs.eg.db)

ego <- enrichGO(
gene=ids$ENTREZID,
OrgDb=org.Hs.eg.db,
pvalueCutoff = 0.05,
ont="BP")

dotplot(ego, showCategory = 15)+
  ggtitle("GO Enrichment Analysis - c_junKO vs c_jun_KO_cDDP24h")
ggsave("GO_plot_c_junKO_vs_c_jun_KO_cDDP24h.png")

```


```{r}
#KEGG
ekegg <- enrichKEGG(
gene=ids$ENTREZID,
organism="hsa")

dotplot(ekegg, showCategory = 15)+
  ggtitle("c_junKO vs c_jun_KO_cDDP24h(KEGG Pathway Analysis)")
ggsave("KEGG_plot_c_junKO_vs_c_jun_KO_cDDP24h.png.png")
```
